missing_units.boundary: src/vfs/storage/replace.py#fuzzy replacers run inline in the writer transaction

excluded_blocks.reason: edit leaves no state that builds up past the call; the cost is CPU while the transaction is held
the edit rights gate (backend.py:729-732, gate.targets modify) runs before edit_rows and is owned by the WriteGate unit

missing_units.reason: The architecture names replace.py's O(n^2) Levenshtein, and the compute unit lists replace.py as a starting path, but none of that unit's four checks or two unresolved items touches edit. In source, block_anchor_replacer (replace.py:167-235) scans forward from every line that matches the first anchor until it finds the last anchor, which is O(L^2) in content lines. It then runs pure-Python levenshtein (replace.py:61-82, a full len(a) x len(b) matrix) on each middle line. line_trimmed_replacer is O(L x F), and each match recomputes start_pos with an O(L) sum. edit_rows (writes.py:261) calls edited_entry for every target, synchronously on the event loop, inside the open writer transaction. Neither the size of the old/new strings nor the number of edits or targets is capped (params has no string-length caps). So any caller with contribute or owner rights on one row can stall the shared loop and hold the store's write lock (on SQLite, every writer).

missing_units.reason: This is a parallel path to grep that the compute unit did not check. Storage grep offloads its verify stage and enforces WALL_TIME_BUDGET (offload.py:1-50). The router's chained grep (base.py:1864-1946) does neither: it reads every absent body through self.read and calls match_texts, which invokes verifier.count_lines/hit_lines with budget=None (grep.py:252,259) synchronously on the event loop. Releasing the GIL does not free the loop thread. That path also reaches the per-hit context duplication candidate with no wall cap at all. A second, distinct root cause from the glob-backtracking candidate is gate cardinality. The globs and globs_not lists are unbounded str_seq values (params.py:251-309), and glean appends one escaped glob per observation (glean.py:261-262). passes_filters/passes_gates then run any() over every gate for every candidate row (glob.py:240-243, scope.py:105-107), and the SQL channel narrowing is dropped when there are more arms than fan_arms (scope.py:160-164). The result is O(candidates x globs) matching on the loop, for batches the 10k contract declares supported.

missing_units.reason: The compute unit checked only glean's limit argument; nobody checked the query string. The query has no length cap (params.py:294). The backend's local-provider embed_query runs embed_batch inline on the event loop (provider.py:131, which says 'its one short text inline'), and asyncio.wait_for at backend.py:676 cannot interrupt synchronous CPU. A hosted provider is called once per distinct query with no per-principal quota, which is operator-owned spend open to anonymous callers. The cache _query_vectors keeps up to 256 entries keyed on the full query string (backend.py:171,672-679), so memory is unbounded per entry. tokenize(query) has no cap on distinct terms, and every term drives lexical_stats IN-list probes, _visible_lexicon and decode_summary/select_blocks (glean.py:257-300,480). Statement count and decode work therefore grow with query size.

Two questions are open. First, any writer can plant .md links (publish_links mints edges even toward targets the author cannot list, a separate candidate) and so raise a chosen entry's prior in every other agent's ranked results, which is retrieval steering. Second, a visible entry's factor reflects edges from rows the caller cannot see, which is an aggregate oracle. The BM25 unit made statistics come from the visible set only; this ranking leg was never held to that rule.

missing_units.reason: The grants read verb has no unit. The grant unit's three checks cover only the grant, revoke and posture writes. list_grants (rights.py:965-1001) selects every grant row on the path and on each of its ancestors. A caller holding read_write at the addressed path, which can come from a grant on its own subtree or from the everyone posture (see the confirmed grant-escalation candidate), gets back all principals' rows on '/' and every intermediate prefix: principal ids, levels, granted_by. A caller without read_write gets its own, group and everyone rows through _own_ids. A unit needs to settle whether showing ancestor rows to a subtree admin is intended. It also needs to check that the not_found arm for list-only, owner-floor and road paths matches a truly absent path.
